IDQ20790
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Major Flood Warning for the Mary River

Issued at 5:31 pm AEST on Sunday 25 October 2026
Flood Warning Number: 7


MAJOR FLOODING POSSIBLE AT TIARO OVERNIGHT INTO MONDAY, WITH PEAK EXPECTED DURING MONDAY
MINOR FLOODING POSSIBLE AT MARYBOROUGH FROM EARLY MONDAY

Rainfall during the last few days has caused river level rises along the Mary River and
tributaries. Minor flooding is occurring at Gympie, where a peak is expected Sunday
evening. The flood peak will then move downstream over the next day or two. Moderate
flooding is occurring at Miva, with a peak expected overnight Sunday into Monday. At
Tiaro, moderate flooding is occurring, with major flooding possible overnight Sunday into
Monday and a peak expected on Monday. Minor flooding is possible at Maryborough from early
Monday, with a peak expected Monday evening.
There is still significant uncertainty in forecast peak heights downstream of Gympie at
this stage with Gympie yet to reach a peak. Forecasts will be refined as peaks are
observed at Gympie, Miva, Tiaro, and other locations.

Mary River to Gympie:
Minor flooding is occurring along the Mary River to Gympie.

No observations are currently available for the Mary River at Dagun Pocket, however the
river level is expected to be above the minor flood level and around a peak. The Mary
River at Dagun Pocket is likely to remain above the minor flood level (7.00 m) overnight
Sunday into Monday.

The Mary River at Gympie is currently at 9.51 m and rising, above the minor flood level
(6.00 m). The Mary River at Gympie may peak near 9.80 m Sunday evening, with minor
flooding.

Six Mile Creek:
Minor flooding is occurring along Six Mile Creek at Cooran Alert.

Mary River downstream of Gympie:
Major flooding is possible along the Mary River downstream of Gympie.

The Mary River at Miva is currently at 12.23 m and rising, with moderate flooding. The
Mary River at Miva is expected to peak above the moderate flood level (9.50 m) overnight
Sunday into Monday. The river may fall below the moderate flood level (9.50 m) Monday
evening.

The Mary River at Tiaro is currently at 11.04 m and rising, with moderate flooding. The
Mary River at Tiaro may exceed the major flood level (12.00 m) overnight Sunday into
Monday. The river may peak above the major flood level (12.00 m) mid-Monday.

The Mary River at Maryborough (Portside) is currently at 3.50 m and steady, below the
minor flood level. The Mary River at Maryborough (Portside) may exceed the minor flood
level (5.00 m) early Monday morning. The river may peak near 5.60 m Monday evening, with
minor flooding. Forecasts will be refined as upstream peaks are observed at Gympie, Miva,
Tiaro, and other locations.

Tinana Creek:
Minor flooding is occurring along Tinana Creek at Tagigan Road.

Safety Advice:
* Don't drive, walk, swim or play in floodwater because it is dangerous.
* Stay away from flooded drains, rivers, streams and waterways.
* Obey road closure signs. Plan ahead so you don't drive on flooded roads.
* Check the ABC and local media for updates. The situation can change quickly, so stay
informed.
* For local emergency management warnings and advice visit
www.disaster.qld.gov.au/warnings.

For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening
emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.

Next issue:
The next warning will be issued by 12:00 AM AEST on Monday 26 October 2026.
